extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors submitting papers to ICML 2025 (main track and position paper track)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and requirements for preparing, anonymizing, submitting, responding to reviews for, and producing camera-ready versions of papers for ICML 2025 (main and position paper tracks). Covers format, page limits, supplementary materials, author responses, camera-ready steps, and related policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main submission page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted papers: main body up to eight pages long; references and appendices may follow and are unlimited in the single PDF. Any submission whose main body goes over the 8 page limit will be automatically rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final versions of accepted papers will be published in the same way; the final camera-ready main paper body may have an extra page (see camera-ready rules). If material is critical to evaluation it must be included in the main body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Camera-ready main page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: In the camera-ready version, you have an extra page to address reviewer comments, so the length limit of the paper body is 9 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledgements, the impact statement, and references are excluded from the 9 page limit. Include appendices as part of the camera-ready PDF; there is NO camera-ready supplementary material of any kind.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF file size limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission PDF maximum size: 50 MB. Camera-ready PDF size limit: 20 MB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If large images cause you to exceed camera-ready limits, reduce size/quality of large images. (Revisions noted in updates clarified submission size limit and camera-ready size.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Required format and typesetting
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must follow the required format specified in the LaTeX style files and example paper; there is no support for any typesetting software other than LaTeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Camera-ready must use the icml2025 LaTeX package with \usepackage[accepted]{icml2025}. No custom macros or other TeX commands; use TeX commands for accents/special characters. Example paper and style zip provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymization / Double-blind reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewing for ICML 2025 is double-blind: submissions must be anonymized and follow the required format; papers that explicitly or implicitly reveal the authors’ identities will be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to prior work in the third person where possible; refrain from including acknowledgements, grant numbers, or links to public code repositories. Previously published overlapping papers must be cited in a way that preserves anonymity and differences explained. If an anonymous reference is needed, include the referred work as Supplementary Material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary Material policy (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: ICML 2025 supports two kinds of supplementary material: supplementary manuscripts and code/data. Supplementary Material must also be anonymized and submitted by the same deadline as the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Traditional text appendices need not be submitted separately because unlimited appendices are allowed in the main submission file. Supplementary Material will not be published or archived and reviewers may choose whether to consult it; critical material must be in the main body. No separate camera-ready supplementary material will be listed on PMLR nor on OpenReview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary code/data specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary code can be submitted as a zip file or a pdf; code must be anonymized (remove author names and licenses). Anonymous GitHub repositories are allowed but must be on a branch that will not be modified after the submission deadline; include the GitHub link in a standalone text file inside the submitted zip.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data submissions are welcome provided authors have the right to do so. There are no format restrictions for supplementary material but authors are responsible for archival and access if they reference it in final version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility / Code encouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to submit code to foster reproducibility. Reproducibility and easy availability of code will be taken into account in the decision-making process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should not include links to non-anonymized repositories; instead submit the code base itself or anonymized repositories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer confidentiality and use restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted papers will not be publicly accessible during review. Reviewers are forbidden from sharing papers they receive for review, or using the material in any way other than to provide their review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are explicitly asked not to seek out external information that might identify authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response process and behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: After initial reviews, authors can respond to reviewer comments during a response period; responses are visible to reviewers after that period. During the subsequent discussion period there is one additional round of communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure of the author response is up to authors (typical to organize by reviewer IDs). Do not include non-anonymized URLs or shortened URLs; reviewers are not expected to follow external URLs in the response. Use professional and polite language, and focus responses on addressing reviewer uncertainty, incorrect assumptions, or misunderstandings. There is no need to respond to every minor suggestion.

rubrics_metrics.name: No revision upload during author feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no option to upload a revised version of the paper during the author feedback period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address substantive points in the author response only; do not attempt version replacement during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review coverage expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: ICML aims to provide three reviews for every paper, although the precise number may vary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer IDs uniquely specify reviewers but are otherwise arbitrary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Camera-ready registration and consent requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: At least one author must register for the conference with the ‘Conference’ option checked; a ‘Virtual Pass’ alone is not sufficient. At least one author needs to digitally sign the ICML 2025 Publishing Release form; the presenting author needs to sign the Recording Release and License form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The corresponding author must sign the PMLR Publication Agreement form and upload it as part of the camera-ready submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Camera-ready required files and form completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the camera-ready form on OpenReview and upload required files (camera-ready PDF, publication agreement, etc.). Enter title and abstract in the camera-ready form exactly matching the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check pdf with ICML format checker; upon successful completion obtain a 5-letter submission code to enter in the camera-ready form. Upload publication agreement and other required signed forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Camera-ready content restrictions and allowances
rubrics_metrics.description: Camera-ready authors may change author order and may slightly change the title and abstract; no author additions are allowed. If you want to change the title significantly, get permission from the program chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may incorporate reviewer-suggested improvements as long as the essential content remains unchanged compared to what reviewers saw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory impact statement in camera-ready
rubrics_metrics.description: Camera-ready PDF must include a mandatory impact statement just before the bibliography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledgements, impact statement, and references are excluded from the 9-page main body limit. For position papers the impact statement is optional but allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lay/plain-language summary requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: New this year: authors will be asked to enter a 'lay summary' (plain language summary) of the paper in the OpenReview form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See linked guidelines and examples for writing lay summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICML format checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Check the PDF file of your paper with the ICML format checker (papercheck.icml.cc) and resolve any detected violations before finalizing camera-ready.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can re-upload until violations are resolved; successful completion yields a 5-letter submission code required in the camera-ready form.

rubrics_metrics.name: No camera-ready supplementary material
rubrics_metrics.description: There is NO camera-ready supplementary material of any kind; camera-ready PDF should include appendices instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want readers to access code or other materials, upload to a repository (e.g., GitHub) and include a link in your paper and/or the optional 'code url' box on OpenReview. Camera-ready supplementary materials will not be listed on PMLR nor on OpenReview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and inclusive language
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to make submissions accessible to people with disabilities and sensory/neurological differences, review guidelines for accessibility to color-blind and visually impaired readers, ensure bibliography is up-to-date, and use inclusive and respectful language when talking about people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow provided accessibility guidelines; inclusive language is expected throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics and font guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer vector graphics (eps or pdf) for experimental results (line plots, bar plots); use bitmap graphics only for illustrations that cannot be represented as vector graphics. This year there is no Type 3 font check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using vector graphics maximizes readability. Citation font size should be the same as that in the main body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper size and abstract formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Your paper must be in US letter size (not A4). Abstracts should be a single paragraph and ideally 4-6 sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow example paper for layout and formatting details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference quality and capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully check references and replace arXiv citations with peer-reviewed papers where possible (arXiv is generally not peer-reviewed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check capitalization in references (e.g., use braces in BibTeX like {Markov} to preserve capitalization of proper names). Ensure bibliography entries include correct names and venues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author-identifying material in responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Author responses and subsequent discussion should not contain information that could reveal the authors’ identities, and should not contain non-anonymized URLs or shortened URLs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses will only be visible to reviewers after the response period; maintain anonymity in all communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of external resources and double-blind caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: It may be possible for reviewers to deduce authors’ identities using external resources (technical reports on the internet); availability of such resources does not constitute a breach of the double-blind policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are explicitly asked not to seek out this information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors wishing to retract an accepted paper must enter a retraction statement in OpenReview; the statement will be reviewed by Program Chairs and all authors contacted. If confirmed, the paper remains on OpenReview but its status is marked as retracted and the retraction statement is publicly visible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow OpenReview procedures to submit the retraction statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy references and additional requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional policies (see Call for Papers) concern dual submissions, use of generative AI tools (including LLMs), ethical conduct for peer review, impact statements, and lay summaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must consult the Call for Papers for full policy details and ensure compliance with those policies.
